clue.text: Criticise a church with a 'miracle cure'

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a church for promoting a supposed miracle cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all claimed to remedy every ill is exactly what a miracle remedy promises.

clue.text: Bluebottles — insects sinking under river

indicators.note: in a down clue, sinking under puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Blowflies and other insects drown beneath the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluebottles' looks like flies to match 'insects', but it is old slang for the police, from their blue uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is dated British slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform.

clue.text: Fairly recent aspiration expressed in (say) Durham?

parts.note: Durham is an example of a place in the North East of England, NE
an aspiration is a wish

explanation.surface: A recent hope voiced in a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a city in North East England, so it exemplifies NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only somewhat new is fairly recent.

clue.text: Dish served in bar once — and badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A meal that used to be served in a pub, and poorly at that.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbonnade is a Flemish beef stew made with beer, a dish.

clue.text: Alarm has a friend stammering

parts.note: a friend is a pal, and stammering repeats its first sound

explanation.surface: Someone's stuttering friend causes alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to shock or dismay them, to alarm them.

clue.text: Tribal chief as executioner?

explanation.surface: Is the leader of the tribe also the man who carries out its sentences?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense: a man who takes heads off, an old variant of headsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A village or tribal leader is called this; it is also an archaic word for the official who beheads.

clue.text: This dream conjured up in a novel

indicators.note: conjured up suggests the letters are magically transformed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dream summoned up inside a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard Times is an 1854 novel by Charles Dickens.

clue.text: A country's former name mostly used in the bigger area around it

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Siam is the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A nation's old name still used for the wider region round it.
explanation.walkthrough: Thailand was once Siam; the continent surrounding it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent that contains Thailand is the larger region around that country.

clue.text: Dominant volunteers in support

parts.note: the main thing is the dominant one
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Leading volunteers are there in a supporting role.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it up, to support it.

clue.text: One over the eight may fall in this activity at the pub?

definitions.text: One over the eight may fall in this activity at the pub?

parts.words: One over the eight may fall in this activity at the pub?
parts.note: one over the eight is slang for a drink too many, but here it is literally the ninth of the pins knocked down in a skittles game

explanation.walkthrough: A drunk might fall over in a pub; in the traditional pub skittles game the ninth pin, one beyond eight, falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub skittles game uses nine pins, so the ninth can be called the one over the eight.

clue.text: Rose? No female to be put down

indicators.note: no female means the letter standing for female is removed from the word

parts.note: a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A rose with no female parts is to be destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the past tense of rise, a natural opposite of the definition, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower something is to bring it down, a direct synonym of put down.

clue.text: Cast characters with pride into hell

indicators.note: the characters (letters) are cast, thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Proud figures in a play are flung into the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdition is eternal damnation, the state of the souls in hell.

clue.text: Dishes of scouse prepared with salt mixed in

indicators.note: the letters are prepared like ingredients, worked into something new
the second word's letters are stirred into the first as part of one rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A recipe: Liverpool stew cooked with salt stirred in.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOUSE is a Liverpool stew; both 'prepared' and 'mixed in' signal the shuffle of SCOUSE plus SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassoulet is a French stew of beans and meat, so several of them are dishes.

clue.text: Dogs for instance will go back a short distance

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: dogs are examples of pets

explanation.surface: The dogs will retreat a little way.
explanation.definitionFit: A pace or stride is a very short distance, as in 'only a step away'.

clue.text: US city produces arts graduate almost coarse in style

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: in puts the trimmed word inside the word for style

parts.note: tone is a manner or style

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rough means coarse

explanation.surface: An American city turns out a crudely stylish arts graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'coarse in style' as a description of the graduate; in fact 'in' is a container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Baton Rouge is the state capital of Louisiana, a city in the USA.

clue.text: A couple of million being sunk in financial problem? That could bring pain

indicators.note: sunk in means one piece is buried inside the other

parts.note: inflation is the economic problem of rising prices
M is million, so two of them give MM

explanation.surface: Losing two million in an economic crisis would be painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Swelling and redness from an injury or infection is the kind of condition that causes pain.

clue.text: Numbers will follow this rule book

definitions.text: Numbers will follow this rule book

parts.words: Numbers will follow this rule book
parts.note: seems to describe a manual of regulations, but Numbers is the book of the Bible that comes straight after this book of laws

explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Numbers follows the third book, which is mainly priestly law.
explanation.definitionFit: The third book of the Old Testament sets out ritual laws, so it is a rule book, and Numbers comes next.

clue.text: Old ships sadly not 'Bristol fashion'?

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, the letters put in poor order

explanation.surface: Old ships are sadly not shipshape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipshape and Bristol fashion' is a British phrase meaning neat and in good order, from the port of Bristol.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless and untidy is the opposite of being in neat seamanlike order.

clue.text: Wanted at home, daughter called on the way up

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: named means called

explanation.surface: Wanted at home: the daughter rang while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns D plus NAMED into DEMAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sought after by many people is wanted.

clue.text: Protracted disunity that was once more common in primary schools

definitions.text: that was once more common in primary schools

parts.note: something protracted is long
division is disagreement or disunity

explanation.surface: Lasting discord that used to be more common in junior classrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests playground quarrels; the definition is the pencil-and-paper arithmetic method, now less taught.
explanation.definitionFit: The written method of dividing large numbers was once a staple of junior-school arithmetic lessons.

clue.text: Wine put on vehicle in seaside resort

parts.note: red is red wine
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Wine loaded onto a car at the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcar is a coastal holiday town in north-east England.

clue.text: Greets Eastern revolutionary, showing respect

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to greet someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: Welcomes an Eastern rebel, showing regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns MEETS plus E into ESTEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard, a synonym of respect.

clue.text: Odd bits of prose taking time — for one used to writing else?

indicators.note: odd bits means the first, third and fifth letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Fragments of prose take time, so a writer might prefer some other form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'else' means something other than the prose just mentioned: the writer works in verse instead. 'Odd bits of' picks P, O, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A versifier is someone accustomed to writing verse rather than prose, the something else the clue means.

clue.text: One up in the air was endlessly stressed, troubled

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed and rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A traveller was stressed and worried without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims WAS to WA; 'troubled' shuffles WA with STRESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight attendant works aloft in an aircraft, a playful way of describing cabin crew.

clue.text: Crop beginning to wilt leading to barren area almost

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a heath is an open area of uncultivated land

explanation.surface: A crop starts to wilt, heading towards near wasteland.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a cereal grown as a farm crop.

clue.text: Case in one truck down under sent north

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent north means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a ute is an Australian word for a pickup truck

explanation.surface: A case packed in a single truck in Australia, sent northward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent north' turns I plus UTE into ETUI.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Nasty teacher — ah, grief!

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: An unpleasant teacher causes a pupil sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish, a synonym of grief.

clue.text: Relation isn't 100% fun, clearly

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters sit concealed within it

explanation.surface: A family member is not entirely enjoyable company.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family relation.

clue.text: Old man passes away? More than one!

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: Father dies? Several of them do!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'Old man': more than one father, so the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the word for father means several fathers, more than one old man.

clue.text: Proposition from those people holding valuable material

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: them refers to those people
ore is rock containing valuable metal

explanation.surface: An offer from a group who own precious resources.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a statement to be proved, a proposition.
